title: Sony Music moves to add more than 30,000 copyrighted recordings to its lawsuit against Udio

reading.body:
The core failure here is training a generative AI system on copyrighted recordings without obtaining licenses from the rights holders. Udio's music generation tool was deployed to users before that foundational question, whether the training data was lawfully acquired, had been resolved. That gap between deployment and legal clearance is where the dispute originated.

Universal Music Group settled its claims and reached a licensing arrangement with Udio, while Warner Music Group did the same. Sony Music pursued separate litigation, alleging the training corpus included more than 30,000 of its recordings, and later filed a further lawsuit covering additional recordings a court had not permitted it to add to the original case. Independent artists filed a copyright class action that a court declined to dismiss. What would have caught this problem before it became litigation is a rights-clearance process applied to training data before the model was built or commercially deployed, not after.

None of the lawsuits against Udio have produced a final judicial finding on liability, and the settlements do not constitute admissions of wrongdoing. Whether Udio's training practices actually violated copyright law remains a question the courts have not fully adjudicated.

summary:
Universal Music Group has settled its lawsuit against AI music startup Udio, reaching licensing agreements that resolve disputes over copyright infringement. UMG had accused Udio of using copyrighted songs, including The Temptations' "My Girl," to train its artificial intelligence system without permission. Udio's technology allows users to create original music from text prompts using AI. The specific financial terms of the settlement were not disclosed.

Under the new agreement, Udio will launch a platform next year trained exclusively on authorized and licensed music, allowing artists to participate and receive compensation. This marks Udio's first licensing deal with a major music label. UMG's CEO stated the company remains committed to supporting artists while embracing new technologies. Additionally, UMG announced a partnership with Stability AI to develop music creation tools for artists and producers.
